messages:
marta: quick brain-dump: i'm prototyping a separate reclaim daemon (reclaimd) that runs out-of-band compaction + slab defrag. main challenge: safe handoff with the in-process evictor. want to land a tiny cross-process lease table over shared mmap with CAS and sequence numbers. thoughts?
arjun: separate process makes sense for crash isolation. what's the lease table shape?
marta: thinking fixed-size array of slab entries. each entry: slab_id, lease_type (none|soft|exclusive), seq, owner_pid, cpu_budget_ms, cooldown_until. use seq for ABA.
nina: do we need futex/wakeup so reclaimd can sleep efficiently when preempted?
dean: yes, futex on seq change is nice. reclaimd holds soft lease and does preemptible chunks; evictor can bump seq+set exclusive to preempt.
ops-bot: note: perf test #137 shows cross-process mmap reads are cheap but write contention spikes when many writers.
marta: plan: reclaimd only writes to its held entries. evictor does single-writer exclusive flips. writers always do atomic compare-and-swap on seq+lease bits. readers can snapshot non-atomically.
arjun: we should define exact CAS ordering to avoid lost-preempt: writer does CAS(seq -> seq+1 with requested flags), then optionally futex_wake. preempt protocol: evictor CAS to exclusive; reclaimd checks seq changed and yields.
nina: how do we handle partial compaction state? reclaimd must checkpoint page lists so if preempted mid-compact we can resume or abort safely. add a compact_checkpoint counter in entry.
dean: and we need permissions so runtime process can't accidentally map a reclaimed region it doesn't own. maybe a simple ownership bit enforced by kernel mprotect after successful lease flip?
marta: kernel ops are heavier. prefer soft enforcement: runtime checks lease table before shy migrations. only on edge cases (mismatch) do we revalidate via kernel checks. keep kernel ops for emergency-exclusive path.
arjun: rollout wise: feature-flag reclaimd=false by default. opt-in hosts get reclaimd with tiny cpu slices (10ms) and long cool-downs. monitor metrics: reclaimd.compact_ops, reclaimd.preemptions, lease.cas_failures, slab.cooldown_hits, host.p99_latency.
nina: metric names look good. add reclaimed_pages_by_host and reclaimed_pages_by_tenant. also track reclaimed_bytes_retained (resident delta).
dean: we need operator controls to dump lease table on demand for debugging: `curl /debug/leases` or `gcore` equivalent. expose as read-only HTTP on localhost.
ops-bot: FYI: config suggestion: `idle_threshold=0.4`, `cpu_slice_ms=20`, `per_slab_cooldown=5m`, `max_concurrent_reclaims=2`.
marta: nice. one more safety: if eviction backlog > X or host.cpu_share < Y, reclaimd should immediately pause. integrate with existing evict-scheduler backpressure counter via shared mmap too.
arjun: what about multi-host coord? avoid compaction storms for tenants spread across hosts. start with per-host only and add leader per hostpool later.
nina: prototype plan: i'll implement the shared mmap layout + atomic CAS helpers and futex wake/park helpers. dean can do the runtime side checks.
dean: i'll add lightweight tests: 1) reclaimd preempted mid-compact, no pages lost; 2) concurrent CAS stress; 3) tenants quotas respected.
marta: writeup later in design doc: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/reclaimd-handoff (WIP). meeting end-to-end: aim to canary in 2 weeks if tests pass. :clock3:
ops-bot: reminder: nightly perf-run scheduled; reclaimd disabled there to keep baseline stable.
